title: Transience of the zero set of a polynomial evaluated on the symplectic representation of the braid group
author: Marc Soret and Marina Ville
work: Random walks and the symplectic representation of the braid group
difficulty_reason: Once the classical inputs are supplied as named prerequisites - A’Campo’s surjectivity of B(n+1) onto Sp(2l,F_p), Diaconis’s convergence criterion for a random walk on a finite group generated as a semigroup by its support, Aschbacher’s simplicity of PSp(2n,F_p), the Lachaud-Rolland point-count bound for algebraic sets over finite fields and the irreducibility of Sp(2l,K) as an algebraic variety - the counted proof still has to assemble a source-local transience theorem for the zero set of an arbitrary integer polynomial on the symplectic representation, which is not a qualification exercise. The author must reduce the braid walk to a walk on the finite group Sp(2l,F_p) through the reduction map Pi_p, verify both Diaconis hypotheses for Sp(2l,F_p) including the exceptional case l=1, p=3 by an explicit computation with the reduced Burau images s_1, s_2 and the complete list of normal subgroups of SL(2,F_3), bound the density of the zero set P_p^{-1}(0) inside Sp(2l,F_p) by combining the order formula for Sp(2l,F_p) with the Lachaud-Rolland estimate on a proper subvariety of dimension at most 2l^2+l-1, and then run the epsilon argument that converts the finite-field density bound into the vanishing, as k tends to infinity, of the probability that the walk hits the zero set at step k. That combination - finite-group equidistribution for a Zariski-dense subgroup image together with a Lang-Weil-type density estimate transferred to a random walk on a braid group - is research-level probability and arithmetic geometry, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
